questions.question: In triangle $PQR$, $PQ = 7\text{ cm}$, $PR = 10\text{ cm}$, and $\angle Q = 40^\circ$. Use the sine formula to determine whether triangle $PQR$ can be formed. If it can, find all possible values of $\angle R$, correct to 3 significant figures.
questions.referenceAnswer:
1. sine formula: $\frac{PR}{\sin Q} = \frac{PQ}{\sin R}$
2. substitute: $\frac{10}{\sin 40^\circ} = \frac{7}{\sin R}$
3. solve for $\sin R$: $\sin R = \frac{7 \sin 40^\circ}{10} = 0.4500$
4. find acute angle: $R = \arcsin(0.4500) = 26.743^\circ$
5. check obtuse possibility: $180^\circ - 26.743^\circ = 153.257^\circ$
6. verify triangle angle sum: $Q + R = 40^\circ + 153.257^\circ = 193.257^\circ > 180^\circ$, so rejected
Answer: $26.7^\circ$

questions.question: In triangle $XYZ$, $XY = 4\text{ cm}$, $YZ = 9\text{ cm}$, and $\angle X = 125^\circ$. Use the sine formula to determine whether triangle $XYZ$ can be formed. Show your reasoning clearly.
questions.referenceAnswer:
1. sine formula: $\frac{YZ}{\sin X} = \frac{XY}{\sin Z}$
2. substitute: $\frac{9}{\sin 125^\circ} = \frac{4}{\sin Z}$
3. solve for $\sin Z$: $\sin Z = \frac{4 \sin 125^\circ}{9} = 0.3642$
4. find acute angle: $Z = \arcsin(0.3642) = 21.362^\circ$
5. check obtuse possibility: $180^\circ - 21.362^\circ = 158.638^\circ$
6. verify triangle angle sum: $X + Z = 125^\circ + 158.638^\circ = 283.638^\circ > 180^\circ$, so rejected; but $125^\circ + 21.362^\circ = 146.362^\circ < 180^\circ$, so valid
Answer: Yes, triangle can be formed

questions.question: In triangle $LMN$, $LN = 5\text{ cm}$, $MN = 8\text{ cm}$, and $\angle L = 110^\circ$. Use the sine formula to find $\angle N$, correct to 3 significant figures. State whether the triangle is ambiguous and explain why.
questions.referenceAnswer:
1. sine formula: $\frac{MN}{\sin L} = \frac{LN}{\sin N}$
2. substitute: $\frac{8}{\sin 110^\circ} = \frac{5}{\sin N}$
3. solve for $\sin N$: $\sin N = \frac{5 \sin 110^\circ}{8} = 0.5878$
4. find acute angle: $N = \arcsin(0.5878) = 36.000^\circ$
5. check obtuse possibility: $180^\circ - 36.000^\circ = 144.000^\circ$
6. verify angle sum: $L + N = 110^\circ + 144.000^\circ = 254^\circ > 180^\circ$, so only one solution
Answer: $36.0^\circ$

questions.question: In triangle $UVW$, $UV = 6\text{ cm}$, $UW = 12\text{ cm}$, and $\angle V = 25^\circ$. Use the sine formula to determine whether triangle $UVW$ can be formed. If not, explain why using the sine ratio.
questions.referenceAnswer:
1. sine formula: $\frac{UW}{\sin V} = \frac{UV}{\sin W}$
2. substitute: $\frac{12}{\sin 25^\circ} = \frac{6}{\sin W}$
3. solve for $\sin W$: $\sin W = \frac{6 \sin 25^\circ}{12} = 0.2113$
4. since $0.2113 < 1$, solution exists
5. find acute angle: $W = \arcsin(0.2113) = 12.189^\circ$
6. check obtuse possibility: $180^\circ - 12.189^\circ = 167.811^\circ$; $V + W = 25^\circ + 167.811^\circ = 192.811^\circ > 180^\circ$, so rejected
Answer: Yes, triangle can be formed

questions.question: In triangle $FGH$, $FG = 9\text{ cm}$, $GH = 6\text{ cm}$, and $\angle H = 30^\circ$. Use the sine formula to find the length of side $FH$, correct to 3 significant figures.
questions.referenceAnswer:
1. sine formula: $\frac{FG}{\sin H} = \frac{GH}{\sin F}$
2. first find $\sin F$: $\frac{9}{\sin 30^\circ} = \frac{6}{\sin F}$
3. solve: $\sin F = \frac{6 \sin 30^\circ}{9} = 0.3333$
4. $F = \arcsin(0.3333) = 19.471^\circ$
5. find $G = 180^\circ - 30^\circ - 19.471^\circ = 130.529^\circ$
6. apply sine formula again: $\frac{FH}{\sin G} = \frac{9}{\sin 30^\circ}$ → $FH = \frac{9 \sin 130.529^\circ}{\sin 30^\circ} = 13.6\text{ cm}$
Answer: $13.6\text{ cm}$
